issue.title: Start-name again rows list a repeated completed Pomodoro name at its first-seen position, not newest-first
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-bc.4 note #8 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, Pomodoro themes epic `suggest` phase); triaged by the bob-cli-bc land agent.

Root cause (verified by reading source at master 7e41788c): `today_start_rows` in `src/native/capture_complete/pomodoros.rs` (lines ~274-291) collects completed entries into `again_entries`, and when a key repeats it replaces the entry *in its first-seen vector slot* (`again_entries[position] = entry`) before the vector is reversed. For a day whose completed Pomodoros are A, B, A (in ledger order), the vector ends as [A(latest), B] and `reverse()` yields [B, A], so the start-name menu (`=#`) offers B before A although A is the most recent session. The logic dates from fa717730d (2026-10-03); bc.4 deliberately preserved Today ordering as PT7 requires, so this is not caused by the themes epic.

Fix: when a repeated key is seen, remove the old slot and push the newer entry (or sort `again` rows by latest occurrence), so `again` rows are newest-first. Add a regression test with a completed A, B, A ledger asserting A precedes B in both `bob capture-complete` (pomodoro_start_name) JSON and the shell presenter. Check the shared menu vectors in tests/fixtures/pomodoro_themes/vectors.json (and the byte-identical bob-plugins copy) still pass or are updated together.

task_type_fields.impact: The most recent completed name sinks below an older one in the Mac Capture, zsh/bash, and Obsidian start-name menus, so re-starting the session you just finished takes extra navigation.
task_type_fields.repro: Today's ledger has completed Pomodoros named A, then B, then A again; run bob capture-complete -c 2 -f json -- '=#' and see the again rows list B before A, although A is the most recent session.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-bc.4 found that completed A, B, A offers B before A in =# completion; it predates the themes epic and needs its own regression-tested fix.
